title: Adjacency powers: which matrix certifies connectivity

located_defect.description: The source (stored source line 0008) argues that a zero entry of A^(n-1) means the two vertices are not connected by a path, so the graph is disconnected. Read over every finite simple graph (matrices over ℕ, entries counting walks) this entrywise statement is the located defect. Supply the corrected matrix criterion, prove the corrected entrywise statement for every finite simple graph, show the criterion is not constant, and prove the source's theorem (line 0001) with the corrected criterion: on a nonempty vertex set G is connected iff the criterion has no zero entry.

/-!

namespace SE_math_994847_q

-- ===== FIXED PART: only the hole «HOLE» may be edited =====
/-- The corrected matrix criterion: a matrix over ℕ computed from the adjacency matrix `G.adjMatrix ℕ` and
the vertex count `Fintype.card V`, whose zero entries certify unreachability (the source uses
`G.adjMatrix ℕ ^ (Fintype.card V - 1)`). The hole must be a matrix expression in `G.adjMatrix ℕ` and
`Fintype.card V` (powers, sums, `1`); it may not mention `Reachable`, `Connected`, `Walk`, `if`/`match`. -/
def criterion {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
    Matrix V V ℕ := «HOLE»

/-- The corrected entrywise claim for every finite simple graph (shape fixed). -/
def CorrectedEntrywise : Prop :=
  ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
    ∀ i j : V, criterion G i j = 0 → ¬ G.Reachable i j
-- ===== END FIXED PART =====

end SE_math_994847_q
